([[The Bronx|The Bronx, New York]]) * [[West Florence High School|West Florence]]
([[Florence, South Carolina]]) | college = * [[Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball|Kansas State]] (2017–2020) * [[Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball|Virginia Tech]] (2020) | draft_year = 2021 | highlights = | years1 = 2021–2022 | team1 = [[AB Contern]] | years2 = 2023–2024 | team2 = [[Cape Town Tigers]] | years3 = 2024–present | team3 = [[Stade Malien (basketball)|Stade Malien]] }} '''Cartier Ducati Diarra''' (born February 6, 1998) is an American-Malian [[basketball]] player who last played for [[Stade Malien (basketball)|Stade Malien]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball|Kansas State Wildcats]] and the [[Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball|Virginia Tech Hokies]]. ==Early life and high school career== Diarra grew up in [[Harlem|Harlem, New York]], and broke his foot at the age of two. His father is from Mali.{{Cite web |last=Moser |first=Megan |date=2018-02-23 |title=I WONDER {{!}} How do I pronounce Diarra's name? |url=https://themercury.com/news/i-wonder-how-do-i-pronounce-diarras-name/article_47b1363e-766e-586e-887d-c4d9e9971cf6.html |access-date=2023-11-28 |website=The Mercury |language=en}} He was mainly raised by his mother, Danyelle Lee, alongside siblings Abraham, Cyncere and LadiRoyale, and rarely spoke to his father. Diarra grew up taking dancing lessons at Uptown Dance Academy. As a freshman, Diarra played basketball for [[Cardinal Hayes High School]] in [[The Bronx|The Bronx, New York]].{{cite web |last1=Woods |first1=Greg |title=The life of Cartier Diarra: How a New York native found his way to the other Manhattan |url=https://themercury.com/k_state_sports/the-life-of-cartier-diarra-how-a-new-york-native-found-his-way-to-the/article_affa1070-fcec-54ff-bf48-f14b4240c6e3.html |website=[[The Manhattan Mercury]] |accessdate=May 9, 2020 |date=November 10, 2017 }}{{Dead link|date=January 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }} After one year, he transferred to [[West Florence High School]] in [[Florence, South Carolina]], where he began living with his aunt, Lillian Shabazz.{{cite web |last1=Moore |first1=CJ |title=The World According to Cartier Diarra |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/1362912/2019/11/12/the-world-according-to-cartier-diarra-kansas-state/ |website=[[The Athletic]] |access-date=May 9, 2020 |date=November 12, 2019}} Diarra joined West Florence's [[varsity team|varsity]] basketball team despite not having much organized basketball experience. As a sophomore, he averaged seven points and 3.7 rebounds per game. Former [[National Basketball Association]] player [[Sharone Wright]], whose son befriended Diarra, became his mentor and father figure.{{cite web |last1=Regan |first1=Brett |title=Diarra's basketball journey steers him to K-State |url=https://kansasstate.rivals.com/news/diarra-s-basketball-journey-steers-him-to-k-state |publisher=KStateOnline |accessdate=May 9, 2020 |date=April 13, 2016}} As a junior, Diarra averaged 12.9 points, 7.6 rebounds, 4.8 assists and 2.2 steals per game. In his senior season, he averaged 18.8 points, 11 rebounds, 7.2 assists, 3.6 steals and 2.1 blocks per game, registering eight [[double (basketball)|triple-doubles]]. Diarra was named ''[[The Morning News (American newspaper)|The Morning News]]'' Player of the Year.{{cite web |last1=Chancey |first1=Scott |title=Boys Basketball Player of Year: West's Diarra credits slick moves on court to dancing background |url=https://www.scnow.com/sports/boys-basketball-player-of-year-wests-diarra-credits-slick-moves-on-court-to-dancing-background/article_fc2caa70-ee54-11e5-8104-d31636a40ea3.html |website=[[The Morning News (American newspaper)|The Morning News]] |accessdate=May 9, 2020 |date=March 20, 2016}} ==College career== ===Kansas State=== Diarra [[redshirt (college sports)|redshirted]] his first season at [[Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball|Kansas State]] after suffering a [[Anterior cruciate ligament injury|torn anterior cruciate ligament]], but recovered quickly and was able to practice with the team and add strength.{{cite web |last1=Robinett |first1=Kellis |title=Bruce Weber sees bright future for K-State guard Cartier Diarra, when he dunks |url=https://www.kansas.com/sports/college/big-12/kansas-state/article180014741.html |website=[[The Wichita Eagle]] |accessdate=May 26, 2020 |date=October 20, 2017}} On November 10, 2017, he made his college debut, recording 13 points and four assists, shooting 4-of-4 from three-point range, in an 83–45 win over [[American Eagles men's basketball|American]].{{cite web |last1=Robinett |first1=Kellis |title=Kansas State throttles American 83-45 in season opener |url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/kansas-state/article184047606.html |website=[[The Kansas City Star]] |accessdate=May 26, 2020 |date=November 10, 2017}} Diarra initially came off the bench but began making an immediate impact as soon as he was placed in a starting role, after Kamau Stokes broke his left foot against [[Texas Tech Red Raiders basketball|Texas Tech]] on January 6, 2018.{{cite web |last1=Robinett |first1=Kellis |title=Cartier Diarra makes a name for himself as K-State point guard |url=https://www.kansas.com/sports/college/big-12/kansas-state/article197133794.html |website=[[The Kansas City Star]] |accessdate=May 26, 2020 |date=January 28, 2018}} On January 13, he scored a freshman season-high 18 points, including 16 in the second half, in a 73–72 loss to 12th-ranked [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]].{{cite web |last1=Bisel |first1=Tim |title=K-State's Cartier Diarra becoming a name to remember — just ask Bill Self |url=https://www.cjonline.com/sports/hawkzone/catzone/2018-01-14/k-state-s-cartier-diarra-becoming-name-remember-just-ask-bill |website=[[The Topeka Capital-Journal]] |accessdate=May 26, 2020 |date=January 14, 2018}} As a freshman, Diarra averaged 7.1 points, 2.5 rebounds and two assists per game. He shot 40.5 percent from three-point range, the third-most by a freshman in program history.{{cite web |title=Cartier Diarra |url=https://www.kstatesports.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/cartier-diarra/6398 |publisher=K-State Athletics |accessdate=May 26, 2020}} Diarra missed eight games of his sophomore season with a broken finger.{{cite web |last1=Green |first1=Arne |title=Wade out, Diarra in for opener |url=https://www.pratttribune.com/news/20190313/wade-out-diarra-in-for-opener |website=[[The Pratt Tribune]] |accessdate=May 26, 2020 |date=March 13, 2019}} On March 15, 2019, at the [[2019 Big 12 men's basketball tournament|2019 Big 12 tournament]] semifinals, he scored a season-high 15 points and grabbed seven rebounds in a 63–59 loss to [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State]]. As a sophomore, Diarra averaged 6.8 points, 3.3 rebounds and 1.7 assists per game. On December 30, during his junior season, he was named [[Big 12 Conference]] Player of the Week, one day after scoring a career-high 25 points to go with seven assists and five rebounds in a 69–67 victory over [[Tulsa Golden Hurricane men's basketball|Tulsa]].{{cite web |last1=Black |first1=Ryan |title=Kansas State guard Cartier Diarra wins Big 12 Player of the Week award |url=https://themercury.com/k_state_sports/kansas-state-guard-cartier-diarra-wins-big-12-player-of-the-week-award/article_26b92623-5281-5799-9465-3c8c89e13179.html |website=[[The Manhattan Mercury]] |accessdate=May 26, 2020 |date=December 31, 2019}} On January 18, 2020, Diarra scored 25 points for a second time, while posting six rebounds and four assists, in an 84–68 win over [[West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball|West Virginia]].{{cite web |last1=Woods |first1=Greg |title=Cartier Diarra lost 7 turnovers against West Virginia, but his playmaking helped K-State win its 1st conference game |url=https://themercury.com/k_state_sports/cartier-diarra-lost-7-turnovers-against-west-virginia-but-his-playmaking-helped-k-state-win/article_824f23e6-8c8a-5aa3-bfb2-9122ee155c0b.html |website=[[The Manhattan Mercury]] |accessdate=May 26, 2020 |date=January 18, 2020}} As a junior, he averaged 13.3 points, 3.8 rebounds, 4.2 assists and 1.8 steals per game. On March 25, 2020, he announced that he would transfer from Kansas State.{{cite web |last1=Rocha |first1=Taylor |title=K-State junior guard Cartier Diarra enters transfer portal |url=https://www.ksn.com/sports/wildcats/k-state-junior-guard-cartier-diarra-enters-transfer-portal/ |publisher=[[KSNW]] |accessdate=May 26, 2020 |date=March 25, 2020 |archive-date=April 24, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200424232543/https://www.ksn.com/sports/wildcats/k-state-junior-guard-cartier-diarra-enters-transfer-portal/ |url-status=dead }} ===Virginia Tech=== On March 31, 2020, Diarra committed to play for [[Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball|Virginia Tech]] in his senior season. He was immediately eligible as a graduate transfer.{{cite web |last1=Arvin |first1=Chris |title=Virginia Tech lands transfer Cartier Diarra |url=https://247sports.com/college/virginia-tech/Article/Virginia-Tech-lands-transfer-Cartier-Diarra-145576015/ |publisher=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |accessdate=May 26, 2020 |date=March 31, 2020}} In four games, Diarra averaged 7.5 points, 2.3 assists and 2.5 rebounds per game. On December 16, 2020, he announced he was opting out of the season, citing concerns over the spread of COVID-19.{{cite news |last1=Barber |first1=Mike |title=Virginia Tech's Cartier Diarra opts out of basketball season, for now |url=https://richmond.com/sports/college/virginia-techs-cartier-diarra-opts-out-of-basketball-season-for-now/article_596a0ba1-5923-5ccb-a410-6ce9aee228ff.html |access-date=June 21, 2021 |work=[[Richmond Times-Dispatch]] |date=December 16, 2020}} == Professional career == After going undrafted in the [[2021 NBA draft]], Diarra made his professional debut with [[AB Contern]] of the [[Luxembourg Basketball League]] in 2020, and averaged 10.4 points in the 2021–22 season.{{Cite news |title=DIARRA Cartier Ducati - Fédération Luxembourgeoise de Basket Ball FLBB |language=fr-BE |work=DIARRA Cartier Ducati - Fédération Luxembourgeoise de Basket Ball FLBB |url=https://www.luxembourg.basketball/joueur/28912/diarra-cartier-ducati/ |access-date=2023-10-24}} In October 2023, Diarra joined South African club [[Cape Town Tigers]] for the [[2024 BAL qualification|2024 BAL qualification tournament]].{{Cite web |title=Instagram |url=https://www.instagram.com/accounts/login/?next=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.instagram.com%2Fthecapetowntigers%2F |access-date=2023-10-24 |website=www.instagram.com}} He was eligible as an African import player due to his Malian heritage.{{Cite web |date=2023-11-26 |title=Cape Town Tigers crowned East Division Elite 16 champions |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/africaleague/2024/qualifiers/news/cape-town-tigers-crowned-east-division-elite-16-champions |access-date=2023-11-28 |website=FIBA.basketball |language=en}} He helped Cape Town qualify for the main tournament, and scored the game-winning basket in the West Division final against [[City Oilers]]. In November 2024, Diarra joined Malian champions [[Stade Malien (basketball)|Stade Malien]] in the [[Road to BAL]].{{Cite web |date=2024-11-06 |title=Stade Malien top Group B, Tripoli extend unbeaten run after Game-day 2 |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/news/stade-malien-top-group-b-tripoli-extend-unbeaten-run-after-game-day-2 |access-date=2024-11-07 |website=www.fiba.basketball |language=en}}
